ideas.title: Nerves before the first fight

evidence.name: Brezo Jr
evidence.hook: Being nervous before your first fight is completely normal. I still get nervous myself, and honestly, that’s not a bad thing.

evidence.name: Brezo Jr
evidence.hook: Nobody tells you what starting MMA really feels like. 👇

evidence.name: The Muay Thai Guy
evidence.hook: This is what I wish I knew when I first started… 👇

ideas.pattern: Someone who has fought tells beginners the honest thing about their first fight: the nerves are normal and don't mean you're not ready.
ideas.why: Likely why: every beginner has the fear and nobody says it out loud, so they save it and send it to the friend with a fight coming up. Three outliers from two creators: 8.6x, 4.9x and 4.7x their own medians (43.6k, 25.0k, 255k views).

version.hook: BEING NERVOUS BEFORE YOUR FIRST FIGHT DOESN'T MEAN YOU'RE NOT READY.
beats: I was 16. It was his sixth fight and my first. (hook word READY flies from behind your head)
Someone told me: if you don't knock him out, you lose. (white card, keyword LOSE)
The nerves aren't a sign you're not ready. They're a sign it matters. (card, keyword MATTERS)
I knocked him out. They called it a draw. Your first fight won't go to plan either, and that's fine.
Close: send this to someone with a fight coming up.
version.needs: Your own words on how the nerves felt (founder.md has the facts of the fight, not the feeling). Headroom above your head when filming.

The swap: phone in the bag, 2 minutes of shadowboxing in silence
Close: try it next session and tell me if your first round feels different
